title: Flat-term derived square for quotient section pull transport
statement: Given normalized endpoint ScalarSectionData, a PullNormalized internal comparison lam, a derived section comparison barLam satisfying the conjugation/realization equation for lam through the endpoint derived comparisons and canonical geometric comparisons, and an ordinary square e satisfying the ordinary realization equation, the scalar-model derived computation equation holds on every flat-term K-flat complex.

proof.text: Use the endpoint all-complex scalar computation equations from ScalarSectionNormalized in the form of section_pull_transport_scalar_computation. Use the canonical section-derived geometric computation equation at each coefficient ring.

Evaluate PullNormalized at the homotopy quotient of an internal cochain complex. Remove the identity homotopy composition factor and identify the remaining homotopy comparison with its localized cochain comparison.

Apply the already proved generic paste_diagram categorical pasting lemma from SectionPullComputationOfRealization to the actual scalar models and their natural counits. Its scalar and geometric side equations are those of step 1; its ordinary equation is he; its internal equation is step 2; its derived realization equation is hbarLam. Naturality moves the middle computation maps, and faithfulness of precomposition by the termwise section equivalence gives the equality on every section complex. Remove the identity target composition factor. No flatness argument or new unresolved lemma is needed. The dependency records reuse of that module’s proved private generic helpers, rather than application of its public section-scalar theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem section_pull_transport_kflat_derived {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (cX : ScalarSectionData a X) (cY : ScalarSectionData a Y)
    (hcX : ScalarSectionNormalized a X cX) (hcY : ScalarSectionNormalized a Y cY)
    (lam : D a Y ⋙ L Λ' f ≅ L Λ f ⋙ D a X) (hlam : PullNormalized a f lam)
    (barLam : cY.model.T ⋙ derivedPullback Λ' f ≅
      derivedPullback Λ f ⋙ cX.model.T)
    (hbarLam : ∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules Λ Y),
      (derivedEquivalence Λ' X).functor.map (lam.hom.app M) ≫
          cX.derived.hom.app ((L Λ f).obj M) ≫
          cX.model.T.map ((scalarSectionPullComparison Λ f).hom.app M) =
        (scalarSectionPullComparison Λ' f).hom.app ((D a Y).obj M) ≫
          (derivedPullback Λ' f).map (cY.derived.hom.app M) ≫
          barLam.hom.app ((derivedEquivalence Λ Y).functor.obj M))
    (e : cY.model.E ⋙ pullback Λ' f ≅ pullback Λ f ⋙ cX.model.E)
    (he : ∀ M : Modules Λ Y,
      (equivalence Λ' X).functor.map ((CondensedRing.pullIso a f).inv.app M) ≫
          cX.ordinary.hom.app ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ f).obj M) ≫
          cX.model.E.map ((pullComparison Λ f).hom.app M) =
        (pullComparison Λ' f).hom.app ((QuotientChange.extension a Y).obj M) ≫
          (pullback Λ' f).map (cY.ordinary.hom.app M) ≫
          e.hom.app ((equivalence Λ Y).functor.obj M)) :
    ∀ P : CochainComplex (modules Λ Y) ℤ,
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)).kFlat P →
      (∀ i : ℤ, ObjectProperty.flat (P.X i)) →
      barLam.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) ≫
          cX.model.T.map ((pullback Λ f).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P) ≫
          cX.model.ε.app (((pullback Λ f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso
            (Iso.refl (pullback Λ f ⋙ cX.model.E)) (.up ℤ)).hom.app P) =
        (derivedPullback Λ' f).map (cY.model.ε.app P) ≫
          (pullback Λ' f).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
            ((cY.model.E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map
            ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso e (.up ℤ)).hom.app P)

statement_change.old_statement: Given normalized endpoint ScalarSectionData, a PullNormalized internal comparison, its conjugated derived section comparison barLam, and an ordinary square e, the scalar-model derived computation equation holds on every flat-term K-flat complex.
statement_change.what: The old Lean statement quantified over an unrestricted barLam and never related it to lam. Twisting barLam by minus the identity changes only the left-hand side of the asserted equation. For identity scalar and geometric maps over integer coefficients, on the regular module in degree zero, the positive and negative choices cannot both satisfy it. Add the missing realization equation. This is already guaranteed by the conjugation construction in the sole caller, whose public theorem and conclusion stay unchanged.
